'''A differential equation''' is an equation which relates an unknown function to its derivatives. 

It has the general form:

{{#content:Q1998}}

== Regular v. differential equation ==

A regular equation such as $x^2=9$ is solved by numbers; a differential equation such as $\dot{y}=2y$ is solved by functions $y$.

<blockquote>
$\dot{y}$ and $y'$ are alternative notations for $\frac{dy}{dx}$
</blockquote>

== Classification ==

=== Order ===

The '''order''' of the equation is the order $n$ of the highest derivative that appears. 

For instance, Newton's second law of motion for a body of mass $m$ at position $r(t)$,

{{#content:Q1583}}

is of order 2 with regard to $\vec r$.

=== Linearity ===

A differential equation is '''linear''' when all of the following conditions are satisfied:

The unknown function and its successive derivatives

* appear only to the first power,
* are never multiplied together,
* and are never the arguments of another function. 

'''Examples:'''

$$
\begin{cases}
\dot{y}=2y & \text{linear} \\
\dot{y}=y^{2} & \text{nonlinear: square of the unknown function y} \\
\ddot{\theta}+\dfrac{g}{L}\sin\theta=0 & \text{nonlinear: sine of the unknown function} \theta(t)
\end{cases}
$$

See [[linear differential equation]] for the mathematical definition and special properties.

=== Ordinary v. partial differential equation ===

A differential equation is '''ordinary''' if there is only one independent variable.

A differential equation is '''partial''' if there are several independent variables.

For example: The heat equation

{{#content:Q1590}}

for the temperature $u(x,t)$ of a one-dimensional metal bar is a partial differential equation.

== Methods of solution ==

No general formula solves all differential equations, just as no general formula solves all algebraic equations.

Some simple differential equations can be solved algebraically:

* '''Ordinary differential equations''': 
** [[1st order ODE|First-order]]: separation of variables, integrating factor
** linear equations with constant coefficients, of the second and higher orders: by their characteristic equation
* '''Partial differential equations''': separation of variables
** First-order: method of characteristics

Some methods exist to transform differential equations that cannot be directly solved into directly solvable forms:

* [[Power series]]
* [[Laplace transform]]

More complex differential equations that cannot be solved algebraically can be analysed otherwise:

* '''Numerical solution''': [[Euler's method]] and its higher-order refinements step along the direction field, when only numbers are required.
* '''Qualitative analysis''': equilibria, stability, and long-term behaviour, read directly from the equation.

<ref>{{#cite:Q1577}}</ref>

== Application ==

Differential equations can describe complex relationships between quantities and their rates of change in nature.

For instance, 

* Newton's second law can be stated as $m\ddot{\mathbf{r}}=\mathbf{F}$
* The decay of a radioactive sample and the growth of an unchecked population both follow $\dot{y}=ky$
* Conduction of heat through a solid is described by the partial differential equation $u_{t}=\alpha u_{xx}$.

<blockquote>
$\ddot{r}$, $u_{t}$ and $u_{xx}$ are alternative notations for $\frac{d^2r}{dt^2}$, $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ and $\frac{\partial^{2}u}{\partial x^{2}}$.
</blockquote>

<ref>{{#cite:Q1981}}</ref>
